_note: The four checks are separate fields rather than an array for the same reason as the wizard's questions: no tool template in the fleet uses {{range}} and introducing one is a shared-vocabulary change (owner ruling 2026-07-29). Unlike the wizard's options these carry no scores, so flattening them costs nothing but a fixed count of four -- which IS a real limitation: adding a fifth check needs a template edit, not a config edit.

tool_intro.fallback: Check your car against these common UK finance return standards:
tool_intro.llm_guidance: One line above the checklist. Say COMMON standards, not 'the' standards: the thresholds below are typical of BVRLA fair-wear-and-tear guidance, but the binding standard is whatever the individual finance agreement says.

check_1.fallback: Any scratches longer than a 2p coin? (25mm)
check_1.llm_guidance: First inspection item. The coin comparison is doing real work -- it lets someone judge the threshold in a car park without a ruler -- and the millimetre figure is there for anyone who has one. Keep both. A non-UK site must replace the coin with a locally recognisable object of a stated size.

check_2.llm_guidance: Second item. Kerbed alloys are among the most commonly charged-for return items.

check_3.fallback: Is the service book missing any stamps?
check_3.llm_guidance: Third item. This is a documentation failure rather than physical damage, and it is deliberately in the list because it is the one people forget and it can cost more than a scratch.

check_4.fallback: Are there any chips in the windscreen?

verdict_heading.llm_guidance: Heading of the box shown once anything is ticked. Keep POTENTIAL. The tool knows only what the visitor ticked; it cannot know what an inspector will charge for, and a heading stating charges as fact would be a claim the tool cannot support.

verdict_body.fallback: Lenders typically charge between £50 - £150 per panel for minor repairs. It is often cheaper to get a "Smart Repair" from a local specialist before handing the car back.
verdict_body.llm_guidance: Body of the verdict box. TWO things to preserve. (1) The hedging -- 'typically' and 'often' -- because both figures are indicative ranges, not quotes. (2) The suggestion names a category of service, not a named supplier, which keeps it guidance rather than a recommendation. This is markup text, not a JavaScript string, so the quotes around Smart Repair are safe here; the same value inside a script would break the tool (see tool-early-settlement).
